claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially has an as-cast and homogenized high-temperature BCC state.
Phase stability of the high-temperature BCC state is governed by a composition-dependent thermodynamic threshold for ordering.
Ordering is activated only when atomic mobility permits Al atoms to rearrange.
Multicomponent alloys characteristically exhibit sluggish atomic diffusion.
Local Al enrichment increases the free-energy difference between disordered BCC and an ordered state until a critical value is reached.
Reaching the critical free-energy difference triggers transformation from disordered BCC to an ordered state such as B2.
Kinetic barriers to atomic diffusion delay the onset of the ordering transformation.
Isothermal aging at 700–900°C thermally activates diffusional processes relevant to ordering.
Ordered regions nucleate through local accumulation and ordering of Al atoms within the BCC matrix.
Selective partitioning of Al supplies a free-energy decrease from the disordered state to the ordered state.
Transformation occurs only when the ordering free-energy benefit exceeds a compositional threshold and sufficient atomic mobility is present.
Aging where diffusion is sufficiently active will cause the initially homogeneous BCC phase to nucleate an ordered secondary phase.
The onset of the ordered phase will correlate with a measurable free-energy drop associated with ordering.
Rapid quenching retains the high-temperature BCC phase without noticeable ordering because insufficient time is available to overcome kinetic barriers.
Below approximately 700°C, diffusion is too limited for the proposed ordering transformation.
Above approximately 900°C, the ordering free-energy difference is too small for the proposed transformation.
The exact critical free-energy threshold and corresponding aging time have not been quantitatively established.
The identity of the ordered phase and the influence of local compositional heterogeneity remain uncertain.
